scope: Three authenticated adaptive MediaMTX 1.21.1 trials with automatic source formats and a 1500 kbit/s producer-to-adapter bottleneck, on local Linux ARM64 Docker. The integrated native-boundary acceptance method is required.
boundaries: All three format ladders, source-target recoveries and all six native boundaries pass. Trials one and three pass all 23 gates. Trial two fails playback because baseline native frozen time increases by 0.231s before any network impairment.
All source and recovery phases have zero native freeze increments after their verified four-second boundary. The baseline failure is unrelated to coarse transition attribution; it remains failed.

The baseline event coincides with a 333.3ms browser callback gap, at most 34.4ms JavaScript timer delay, and producer pacer maxima increasing to 200.252ms queued / 165.622ms admitted with 90 queued packets. No packet loss, NACK or decoded frame drop is reported at that sample. Cause is not established.

The containing three-second resource observation has producer/browser/distributor CPU ratios of 1.0512/0.4751/0.5928 cores. This correlation is not proof of host scheduling, encoder or transport causality.
Preserve the failed result and unchanged disruption/continuity budgets. Measurements do not qualify physical capture/display, real OAuth, TURN or target hardware performance.
